title: Open restriction of the counit-defined exceptional tensor map
statement:
Use the finite coefficient conventions [def-trf-coefficient-conventions], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $A=A_{E,n}$, on the small pro-etale sites. Let $G:U^*\to V^*$ and $g:U\to V$ be separated finite-type morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let $u:U\hookrightarrow U^*$ and $v:V\hookrightarrow V^*$ be open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] with $Gu=vg$. Use the constructible adjunctions and exceptional composition of [def-trf-admissibility]. Identify $u^!$ with $u^*$ and $v^!$ with $v^*$ as right adjoints of extension by zero, using the open adjunctions $u_!\dashv u^*$, $v_!\dashv v^*$ of [prop-exc-open-adjoint], and write
$$\kappa_M:u^*G^!M\xrightarrow{\sim}g^!v^*M,\qquad \lambda_N:u^*G^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}g^*v^*N$$
for the resulting exceptional and ordinary composition isomorphisms. For any such morphism $h$, define $T_h:h^!M\otimes h^*N\to h^!(M\otimes N)$ as the exceptional adjunct of
$$Rh_!(h^!M\otimes h^*N)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_h^{-1}}Rh_!h^!M\otimes N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_h^!\otimes1}M\otimes N,$$
using the normalized projection map of [def-exchange-projection], invertible on these domains by [prop-functor-package](5). For $M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(V^*,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the identity
$$\kappa_{M\otimes N}\circ u^*T_G(M,N)=T_g(v^*M,v^*N)\circ(\kappa_M\otimes\lambda_N)$$
holds after the canonical pullback--tensor identifications. No Cartesian hypothesis on the open square and no properness hypothesis on $g$ or $G$ is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.2(a), first sentence of the proof (locality of the exceptional tensor diagram); explicit open-restriction lemma for the normalized finite-coefficient operations

proof.text:
Put $H=Gu=vg$. All functors in this proof are at the fixed finite coefficient ring $A$, and suppress derived symbols. Pullback preserves $D^b_{ctf}$ by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], tensor preserves it by [lem-sf-tensor-ctf], and exceptional preservation is part of the constructible datum [def-trf-admissibility]. Thus every displayed projection is evaluated on its allowed domains. Write
$$c_P:u^*G^!P\xrightarrow{\sim}H^!P,\qquad d_P:g^!v^*P\xrightarrow{\sim}H^!P.$$
These are the inverses of exceptional composition, with the open identifications from [prop-exc-open-adjoint]. Since these comparisons are conjugates of compact-support composition, [lem-trf-adjoint-mate](2) identifies their counits with those of the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. In particular $\kappa_P=d_P^{-1}c_P$. Ordinary pullback composition [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identifies both $u^*G^*N$ and $g^*v^*N$ with $H^*N$; its comparison between them is precisely $\lambda_N$.

source.place: Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits, and Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; agent setup of the two factorizations in Varshavsky Lemma 4.2.2(a)

proof.text: For $j=u,v$, the map $T_j(P,Q)$ is the canonical tensor comparison $j^*P\otimes j^*Q\cong j^*(P\otimes Q)$. Indeed [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] says that the inverse of the open projection $\gamma_{K,Q}:j_!K\otimes Q\to j_!(K\otimes j^*Q)$ is the adjunct of the open unit $K\to j^*j_!K$, tensored with $1$. At $K=j^*P$, transpose $(\varepsilon_{j,P}\otimes1)\gamma_{j^*P,Q}^{-1}$. The result is the tensor comparison preceded by $(j^*\varepsilon_{j,P}\circ\eta_{j,j^*P})\otimes1$, which is the identity by the triangle identity of $j_!\dashv j^*$ [prop-exc-open-adjoint]. This is exactly the defining adjunct of $T_j$, using the normalized open projection of [def-exchange-projection]: for the compactification $(j,\operatorname{id})$ of $j$ the map $\pi_{\operatorname{id}}$ is the identity, so $\operatorname{PF}_j^{(j,\operatorname{id})}=\gamma$, and the compatibility of $\operatorname{PF}$ with compactification comparisons in [fix-prop-projection-formula] makes this independent of the chosen compactification. This calculation takes place on the ordinary derived categories, so also on the full constructible domains.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; open-adjunction normalization supplied by lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization; agent triangle-identity calculation

proof.text:
Set $K=u^*G^!M$ and let $E_G=u^*T_G\circ T_u(G^!M,G^*N)$, with source $K\otimes H^*N$. Transpose $E_G$ under $G_!u_!\dashv u^*G^!$. The composite-counit formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], naturality of the open counit, and the defining adjunct of $T_u$ first give
$$\varepsilon_G\,G_!T_G\,G_!(\varepsilon_{u,G^!M}\otimes1)\,G_!(\operatorname{PF}_{u,K,G^*N}^{-1}).$$
Replace $\varepsilon_GG_!T_G$ by $(\varepsilon_{G,M}\otimes1)\operatorname{PF}_{G,G^!M,N}^{-1}$, the definition in the item. Naturality of projection in its first argument moves $G_!\varepsilon_{u,G^!M}$ through this inverse projection. The adjunct becomes
$$(\varepsilon_{G,M}\,G_!\varepsilon_{u,G^!M}\otimes1)\operatorname{PF}_{G,u_!K,N}^{-1}\,G_!(\operatorname{PF}_{u,K,G^*N}^{-1}).$$
The naturality and composition compatibility asserted in [fix-prop-projection-formula] identify the last two factors with $\operatorname{PF}_{H,K,N}^{-1}$ under $G_!u_!\cong H_!$. Counit compatibility of $c$ [lem-trf-adjoint-mate] identifies the first factor with $\varepsilon_{H,M}H_!c_M\otimes1$.

source.place: Naturality and composition compatibility of PF; agent expansion for H=Gu of Varshavsky Lemma 4.2.2(a), locality

proof.text:
By naturality of $\operatorname{PF}_H^{-1}$, the map at the end of Step 3,
$$(\varepsilon_{H,M}H_!c_M\otimes1)\operatorname{PF}_{H,K,N}^{-1},$$
is the $H_!\dashv H^!$ adjunct of $T_H(M,N)\circ(c_M\otimes1)$. The hom bijection and the counit normalization of $c$ therefore give
$$c_{M\otimes N}\,E_G=T_H(M,N)(c_M\otimes1).$$
Here the passage between the composite and $H$ adjunctions is the conjugate comparison specified by [def-trf-admissibility]; its action on adjuncts is [lem-trf-adjoint-mate](2). No base-change transformation is used.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; agent application of the adjunction bijection

proof.text:
Now set $L=g^!v^*M$ and $E_v=g^!T_v(M,N)\circ T_g(v^*M,v^*N)$. Transpose under $v_!g_!\dashv g^!v^*$. The composite counit [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and naturality of the $g$-counit give $\varepsilon_v\,v_!T_v\,v_!(\varepsilon_g\,g_!T_g)$. Substituting the two defining adjuncts from [def-exchange-projection] and the item, and moving $v_!\varepsilon_{g,v^*M}$ through the first inverse projection by naturality, gives
$$(\varepsilon_{v,M}\,v_!\varepsilon_{g,v^*M}\otimes1)\operatorname{PF}_{v,g_!L,N}^{-1}\,v_!(\operatorname{PF}_{g,L,v^*N}^{-1}).$$
Composition compatibility in [fix-prop-projection-formula] converts the last two factors into $\operatorname{PF}_{H,L,N}^{-1}$. Counit compatibility of $d$ [lem-trf-adjoint-mate] converts the first factor into $\varepsilon_{H,M}H_!d_M\otimes1$. Naturality of $\operatorname{PF}_H^{-1}$ and the hom bijection consequently yield
$$d_{M\otimes N}\,E_v=T_H(M,N)(d_M\otimes1).$$

source.place: Naturality and composition compatibility of PF; agent expansion for H=vg of Varshavsky Lemma 4.2.2(a), locality

proof.text: Step 2 identifies $E_G$ with $u^*T_G$ after the source tensor comparison and identifies $E_v$ with $T_g(v^*M,v^*N)$ after the target tensor comparison. Precompose the equation in Step 5 with $\kappa_M\otimes\lambda_N$. Since $d_M\kappa_M=c_M$ and $\lambda_N$ identifies the two copies of $H^*N$, its right side is $T_H(c_M\otimes1)$, which is the right side of Step 4. Cancel the isomorphism $d_{M\otimes N}$ from the resulting equality and use $d_{M\otimes N}^{-1}c_{M\otimes N}=\kappa_{M\otimes N}$. This gives exactly the required identity. Only the equality of composites $Gu=vg$ was used; neither a Cartesian square nor properness enters.
